S.FORM: ʔuuna=kani miana ma-maruraŋ mata-cuvu-cuvuŋu kara-paʔici.
S.PHON: ʔuunakani miana mamaruraŋ mataʦuvuʦuvuŋu karapaʔitʂi
S.FORM: 'uunakani miana mamarurang matacuvucuvungu karapa'ici.
S.PHON: ʔuunakani miana mama[r|ɾ]u[r|ɾ]aŋ mataʦuvuʦuvuŋu ka[r|ɾ]apaʔitʂi
S.TRANSL: In the past, the old people gathered together drinking.

S.FORM: makasua=kani kara-paʔici para-cani, mia-ranau-ini i-vatu=kani ma-manu sa-saruanai.
S.PHON: makasuakani karapaʔitʂi paraʦani miaranauini ivatukani mamanu sasaruanai
S.FORM: makasuakani karapa'ici paracani, miaranauini ivatukani mamanu sasaruanai.
S.PHON: makasuakani ka[r|ɾ]apaʔitʂi pa[r|ɾ]aʦani mia[r|ɾ]anauini ivatukani mamanu sasa[r|ɾ]uanai
S.TRANSL: While they were singing and drinking, a group of young men came to them.

S.FORM: kacaua si tia=tu-a-papa kara-paʔici.
S.PHON: kaʦaua ʂi tiatuapapa karapaʔitʂi
S.FORM: kacaua si tiatuapapa karapa'ici.
S.PHON: kaʦaua ʂi tiatuapapa ka[r|ɾ]apaʔitʂi
S.TRANSL: Many people wanted to join them drinking.

S.FORM: si ma-naasə mia-iisua ia, ʔuuna nannakə.
S.PHON: ʂi manaasə miaiisua ia ʔuuna nannakə
S.FORM: si manaase miaiisua ia, 'uuna nannake.
S.PHON: ʂi manaase miaiisua ia ʔuuna nannake
S.TRANSL: Perhaps because there were women at that time.

S.FORM: makasua=kani "a-pa-suluvai=ku vuuku=mu, tu-tasiʔarə ia, pir-aiʔ-ini kamua," misa.
S.PHON: makasuakani apasuɾuvaiku vuukumu tutaʂiʔarə ia piraiʔini kamua misa
S.FORM: makasuakani "apasuruvaiku vuukumu, tutasi'are ia, pirai'ini kamua," misa.
S.PHON: makasuakani apasu[r|ɾ]uvaiku vuukumu tutaʂiʔa[r|ɾ]e ia pi[r|ɾ]aiʔini kamua misa
S.TRANSL: They said, "Please lend me your cloth belt. I'll return it to you tomorrow morning."

S.FORM: misa=kani sua sa-saruanai iisa, "ruru-vana ia, i-vat-a ʔi-na tanasa-an=mia" misa=kani.
S.PHON: misakani sua sasaruanai iisa ruruvana ia ivata ʔina tanasaanmia misakani
S.FORM: misakani sua sasaruanai iisa, "ruruvana ia, ivata 'ina tanasaanmia" misakani.
S.PHON: misakani sua sasa[r|ɾ]uanai iisa [r|ɾ]u[r|ɾ]uvana ia ivata ʔina tanasaanmia misakani
S.TRANSL: The young men said, "Come to our house in the evening."

S.FORM: m-iacuʔu=kani maamia nuŋunuŋu.
S.PHON: miaʦuʔukani maamia nuŋunuŋu
S.FORM: miacu'ukani maamia nungunungu.
S.PHON: miaʦuʔukani maamia nuŋunuŋu
S.TRANSL: They said so pointing to the stream.

S.FORM: sua ma-manu nannakə mu-kusa ʔinia c<um>əʔəra.
S.PHON: sua mamanu nannakə mukusa ʔinia ʦuməʔəra
S.FORM: sua mamanu nannake mukusa 'inia c<um>e'era.
S.PHON: sua mamanu nannake mukusa ʔinia ʦumeʔe[r|ɾ]a
S.TRANSL: Young ladies went there to look at it.

S.FORM: ʔaisi=kani cikiriŋa nuŋunuŋu sua takarura, ni-mati-kusa=kani na vuuku.
S.PHON: ʔaiʂikani tʂikiriŋa nuŋunuŋu sua takarura nimatikusakani na vuuku
S.FORM: 'aisikani cikiringa nungunungu sua takarura, nimatikusakani na vuuku.
S.PHON: ʔaiʂikani tʂiki[r|ɾ]iŋa nuŋunuŋu sua taka[r|ɾ]u[r|ɾ]a nimatikusakani na vuuku
S.TRANSL: The frogs were holding on to the cloth belt by the shore of the stream.

S.FORM: mu-ʔiarə=kani sua nannakə mati-saaʔə sua vuuku ma-livulaʔə na ra-vatu-vatu-a.
S.PHON: muʔiarəkani sua nannakə matisaaʔə sua vuuku maɾivuɾaʔə na ravatuvatua
S.FORM: mu'iarekani sua nannake matisaa'e sua vuuku marivura'e na ravatuvatua.
S.PHON: muʔia[r|ɾ]ekani sua nannake matisaaʔe sua vuuku ma[r|ɾ]ivu[r|ɾ]aʔe na [r|ɾ]avatuvatua
S.TRANSL: The young ladies grabbed the cloth belt slowly and hit it on some rocks.

S.FORM: ma-ala sua vuuku-ini mu-caanə.
S.PHON: maaɾa sua vuukuini muʦaanə
S.FORM: maara sua vuukuini mucaane.
S.PHON: maa[r|ɾ]a sua vuukuini muʦaane
S.TRANSL: They took the cloth belt and left.

S.FORM: tee=tasiʔarə=ci i-vatu=kani sua ma-manu sa-saruanai.
S.PHON: teetaʂiʔarətʂi ivatukani sua mamanu sasaruanai
S.FORM: teetasi'areci ivatukani sua mamanu sasaruanai.
S.PHON: teetaʂiʔa[r|ɾ]etʂi ivatukani sua mamanu sasa[r|ɾ]uanai
S.TRANSL: The young men came in the morning.

S.FORM: "ni-m-i-kai-naanu sua navuŋu=mu?"
S.PHON: nimikainaanu sua navuŋumu
S.FORM: "nimikainaanu sua navungumu?"
S.PHON: nimikainaanu sua navuŋumu

S.FORM: m-ali-vali=kani sua saruanai, "kaʔanə=kamu tavalaʔə mia ru-vana ia, ni-ala=mu sua vuuku ma-livulaʔə ra-vatu-vatu-a," misa=kani sua saruanai. "sua iisua ia, iikimi," misa.
S.PHON: maɾivaɾikani sua saruanai kaʔanəkamu tavaɾaʔə mia ruvana ia niaɾamu sua vuuku maɾivuɾaʔə ravatuvatua misakani sua saruanai sua iisua ia iikimi misa
S.FORM: marivarikani sua saruanai, "ka'anekamu tavara'e mia ruvana ia, niaramu sua vuuku marivura'e ravatuvatua," misakani sua saruanai. "sua iisua ia, iikimi," misa.
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]ikani sua sa[r|ɾ]uanai kaʔanekamu tava[r|ɾ]aʔe mia [r|ɾ]uvana ia nia[r|ɾ]amu sua vuuku ma[r|ɾ]ivu[r|ɾ]aʔe [r|ɾ]avatuvatua misakani sua sa[r|ɾ]uanai sua iisua ia iikimi misa
S.TRANSL: The young men replied, "Didn't you know it was you who took the cloth belt and hit on the rocks in the evening?" "It is us," they said.
